title: Flip Up to the First Marker Letter
statement:
You get a lowercase string word and a letter ch. Find the first position where ch occurs and reverse the part of word from the start up to and including that position. The rest of the string stays as it is.

If ch does not occur in word, return word unchanged.

examples.why: The first k is at index 4, so "stack" is reversed into "kcats" and "atlas" stays.
The first a is at index 0. Reversing a single character changes nothing; using the last a would reverse the whole word.
There is no z, so nothing is reversed.

constraints: word and ch are lowercase letters
hints: First find where to stop. Which built-in finds the first occurrence of a character?
Reversing a range in place is a classic two-pointer job: swap the two ends, then move both inward.
If there is no occurrence, the index is -1 and there is nothing to reverse.

explain.intuition:
Two small jobs: find the first ch, then reverse everything up to it. indexOf gives the first position, or -1 if there is none.

For the reversal, put one pointer at 0 and one at that position, swap the characters, and step both pointers toward each other until they meet. Strings are immutable in JavaScript and Python, so do the swaps on a character array and join it at the end, or simply build reversed(prefix) + rest.
steps: Copy the word into a character array.
Set i = 0, j = k; while i < j, swap positions i and j, then i++, j--.
Join the array and return it.
pitfalls: Using the last occurrence (lastIndexOf) instead of the first one.
Reversing up to but not including ch: the marker letter itself moves to the front.
Reversing the whole word when ch is missing, because -1 was used as an end index.

solutions.title: Slice, reverse, glue
solutions.idea: Reverse the prefix up to the first ch with built-ins and attach the untouched rest.

solutions.title: Two pointers on a character array
solutions.idea: Swap the ends of the prefix and move inward until the pointers meet.

followups: Reverse the segment between the first and second occurrence of ch instead.
Apply many prefix reversals in a row. How could you avoid touching every character each time?
